content.text:
This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Utility 2 is out of service, so standby generator G1 is running and carries every load it is connected to through closed breakers. Then main breaker 52-M1 trips. The operator restores power with this procedure: (1) find the loads that were running before the trip and lost power; (2) tie breaker 52-T (now open) will be closed, which re-energizes only what can then be reached from G1 through closed breakers; (3) G1's rating is printed next to it on the drawing; if G1's total load after closing 52-T would exceed that rating, the operator first opens the load breakers of loads that 52-T would restore, one at a time, largest kW first, until the total is at or below the rating; (4) the operator closes 52-T. No other breaker changes position. A load behind an open breaker was not running before the trip. What is the total kW of the loads that were running before the trip and are not running at the end (loads shed in step 3 plus loads 52-T cannot reach)? Answer with an integer number of kW.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
**Answer: 682 kW**

**1. Loads running before the trip (and lost).** 52-M1 feeds Bus 1, and 52-ET (closed) ties Bus 2 and Bus E to G1. Bus 2B is fed from Bus 1 through closed CB-04, and CB-06 is open. The loads on Bus 1 and Bus 2B that were running and are now dead are:
- PP-2 139 kW (CB-11), HP-2 67 kW (CB-12), via CB-02
- DH-B 345 kW (CB-14) and KP-1 87 kW (CB-15), via CB-03 to Bus 1B
- CHWP-1 47 kW (CB-16), EL-1 40 kW (CB-17), AC-1 111 kW (CB-18), via CB-04 to Bus 2B

Not running before the trip: LAB-2 (CB-01 open) and BP-1 (CB-13 open).

**2. Reach of 52-T.** Closing 52-T ties Bus 1 to Bus 2, which G1 already feeds through 52-ET. All seven lost loads above are reachable, so 52-T restores them all.

**3. G1 load check.** Before 52-T closes, G1 carries EV-1 150 kW (CB-08), CT-1 70 kW and EF-4 17 kW (via CB-07 to Bus EB), and FP-1 77 kW (CB-10). That is 314 kW. Adding the restored loads gives 314 + 836 = 1150 kW, which exceeds the 525 kW rating.

Shedding restored loads, largest first:
- Open DH-B (345): 1150 − 345 = 805 kW
- Open PP-2 (139): 666 kW
- Open AC-1 (111): 555 kW, still above 525
- Open KP-1 (87): 468 kW, at or below 525, so stop

Shed in step 3: 345 + 139 + 111 + 87 = 682 kW.

**4. Loads 52-T cannot reach.** None. Every lost running load is reachable, so this contributes 0 kW.

Total lost at the end: 682 + 0 = 682 kW.

FINAL ANSWER: 682

I'm going through the one-line diagram: Utility 1 feeds BUS 1 through 52-M1, while 52-M2 looks open, so BUS 2 isn't energized from the main feed and Utility 2 is out of service anyway. Bus E gets its power from G1 through a closed 52-G1, and I'm now moving on to the 52-ET breaker.

I'm tracing the power path now: with 52-ET closed, G1 reaches Bus 2 and Bus E, and since 52-T is open, nothing crosses from Bus 1 to Bus 2. Then I'm checking which loads on Bus 1 lose power when 52-M1 trips, starting with CB-02 feeding the HP and PP loads through CB-11 and CB-12.

I'm checking the breakers that feed the loads on Bus 1: CB-11 and CB-12 both come off the CB-02 bus, so the PP and HP loads are running, and CB-03 and CB-15 are also closed and carrying their loads.

I'm checking the Bus 2B feed: CB-04 is closed and runs from Bus 1 over to Bus 2B, while the CB-05 tie to Bus 1B is open. Next I'm looking at which loads on Bus 2B are energized, starting with CB-16 feeding CHWP-1.

I'm checking the rest of the Bus 2B and Bus EB feeds: CB-06 on Bus 2B is open, and CB-07 carries Bus 2 over to Bus EB, which is closed. Next I'm looking at CB-08 and the EV-1 load it feeds.

I'm checking the Bus 2 side now: CB-09 is open, so nothing reaches the Bus EB load there. CB-10 is closed and feeds FP-1 on Bus E, which is running. On Bus EB, CB-19 and CB-20 are closed and carry CT-1 and EF-4, fed from Bus 2 through the closed CB-07.

I'm checking the Bus 2B feed again: CB-06 links Bus 2 to Bus 2B and is open, so Bus 2B is only fed from Bus 1 through CB-04. I'm also noting that Bus 2 is still energized from G1 through the closed 52-ET, even though 52-M2 is open.

Now I'm working out what happens to Bus 2B and Bus 1 when 52-M1 trips: Bus 2B loses its feed through CB-04 because Bus 1 goes dead, and it has no other path since CB-06 is open. Then I'm checking which Bus 1 loads drop, with PP-2 and HP-2 lost and LAB-2 and BP-1 already not running.

I'm now looking at what happens if 52-T closes: it ties Bus 1 to Bus 2, which G1 keeps energized through the closed 52-ET. That would bring Bus 1 back, and with CB-02 closed the PP-2 and HP-2 loads on it would be restored, while CB-01 stays open.

I'm working through which loads the 52-T tie would bring back once Bus 1 is energized again from G1. The lost loads are PP-2, HP-2, DH-B, KP-1, CHWP-1, EL-1 and AC-1, and I'm checking whether any of them were not already running before the trip.

I'm adding up the load G1 carries right now, before 52-T closes: the EV-1 at 150 kW on Bus 2, the CT-1 and EF-4 loads on Bus EB at 87 kW together, and FP-1 at 77 kW on Bus E. That comes to about 314 kW.

I'm checking the remaining load: the 314 kW G1 carries before 52-T closes, and I'm confirming that Bus EB stays separate from Bus E, since CB-09 is open and 52-ET only links Bus 2 to Bus E.

I'm adding the lost loads that 52-T would restore, which brings the total to about 1150 kW against the 525 kW rating. So I need to shed load, starting with the largest loads on the restored side: DH-B at 345 kW first, then PP-2, AC-1, and the rest in order.

I'm working out the load to shed: DH-B at 345 kW goes first, then PP-2 at 139 kW, and AC-1 at 111 kW, which brings the total from 1150 kW down to about 555 kW. KP-1 at 87 kW would take it under the 525 kW rating.

I'm adding up the shed loads, DH-B, PP-2, AC-1 and KP-1, which come to 682 kW. The remaining restored loads, HP-2, CHWP-1 and EL-1, bring the G1 total to about 468 kW, which is under the 525 kW rating. I'm also checking that every running load on the restored side is reachable through the tie, since the only open breakers, CB-06 and CB-13, aren't carrying running loads.

I'm checking whether any remaining loads were running before the trip and might have been missed. BP-1, LAB-2 and EV-1 are all accounted for, so the 682 kW shed looks complete.

I'm settling on the answer: shedding DH-B, PP-2, AC-1 and KP-1 brings the load down to the rating, so the total shed is 682 kW.
